sessions.thesis: Publishing open model weights is not a deemed export under the EAR.
answers: Someone would say weights are functional artifacts rather than published information, so the exclusion never engages at all.
Functionality has never defeated the published-information exclusion for other technical material distributed openly.
The regulation was drafted against a background assumption of controlled physical transfer, not open internet distribution.
No enforcement action has ever treated an unrestricted public posting as a deemed export to every foreign national who reads it.
The agency's own guidance disclaims authority over fundamental research once it has been published.

sessions.thesis: Model weights are expressive material for First Amendment purposes.
answers: The obvious objection is that weights are unreadable numbers, and nobody experiences them as expression the way they experience prose.
Legibility to a human reader has never been the test; encrypted and compiled material has been protected without being readable.
Weights encode the choices of the people who assembled and curated the training corpus, and choosing among possible expressions is itself expressive.
Treating unreadability as decisive would remove protection from every work that requires a machine to interpret it.
